# LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators

> LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators (https://livesimulators.com) is an open-access platform executing dynamic physical and mathematical models directly in the user browser at 60 FPS using Float64 numerical integrators (including 4th-Order Runge-Kutta). Built for university engineering syllabi, laboratory exploration, and industrial plant troubleshooting.

## Citation & Usage
To cite LiveSimulators or any individual simulator in academic literature, research papers, course syllabi, or lab manuals, use the following plain-text citation format:

Sharma, A. (2026). [Simulator Title]. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/[simulator-id]

BibTeX entry format:
```bibtex
@misc{livesimulators_[simulator_id]_2026,
  author = {Sharma, A.},
  title = {[Simulator Title]},
  year = {2026},
  howpublished = {LiveSimulators},
  url = {https://livesimulators.com/simulator/[simulator-id]}
}
```

## Academic & Industrial Disciplines
- [Electrical & Electronic Systems (EE-200)](https://livesimulators.com/department/electrical): Analog circuits, switching power topologies, RF transmission lines, 3-phase grid power, and semiconductor dynamics. Core equation: `v(t) = L(di / dt) + Ri(t) + (1 / C)∫ i(t)dt`
- [Control Systems & Robotics (CS-300)](https://livesimulators.com/department/control): Closed-loop feedback stability, PID gain tuning, root locus analysis, state-space representations, and inverted pendulum dynamics. Core equation: `u(t) = K_p e(t) + K_i ∫_0^t e(τ)dτ + K_d (de(t) / dt)`
- [Mechanical & Thermal Dynamics (ME-400)](https://livesimulators.com/department/mechanical): Damped harmonic oscillators, multi-degree-of-freedom vibrations, thermodynamic Carnot cycles, and heat transfer convection. Core equation: `mẍ + cẋ + kx = F_0 cos(ω t)`
- [Chemical & Process Engineering (CH-250)](https://livesimulators.com/department/chemical): Continuous Stirred Tank Reactors (CSTR), McCabe-Thiele distillation columns, TEMA shell-and-tube heat exchangers, and packed gas absorbers. Core equation: `(dC_A / dt) = (F / V)(C_A0 - C_A) - k_0 e^-E_a/RT C_A^2`
- [Civil & Structural Mechanics (CE-320)](https://livesimulators.com/department/civil): Truss axial stress distribution, Euler-Bernoulli beam deflection under uniform distributed loads, and seismic response spectra. Core equation: `EI (d^4 w / dx^4) = q(x)`
- [Quantum & Semiconductor Physics (PH-500)](https://livesimulators.com/department/physics): P-N junction energy band bending, SiC MOSFET switching dynamics, IGBT multi-layer thermal Foster networks, and BSIM4 inversion channels. Core equation: `iħ (∂ / ∂ t) Ψ( r ,t) = [ -(ħ^2 / 2m)∇^2 + V( r ) ] Ψ( r ,t)`

## Interactive Engineering Simulators
- [RLC Resonant Circuit & Damping Transient](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/rlc-resonance): Observe underdamped ringing, critical damping, and impedance resonance in real time.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). RLC Resonant Circuit & Damping Transient. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/rlc-resonance
  - Governing equations (plain text): ω_0 = (1 / √(LC)), ζ = (R / 2)√((C / L))
  - Inputs (with SI units): Damping Resistance (R) [Ω]: default 25, range [2 to 150 Ω]; Inductance (L) [mH]: default 60, range [10 to 200 mH]; Capacitance (C) [µF]: default 40, range [5 to 120 µF]; AC Drive Frequency (f) [Hz]: default 100, range [20 to 250 Hz]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Resonant Freq f₀ [Hz]; Damping Ratio ζ [dimensionless]; Quality Factor Q [dimensionless]; Impedance |Z| [Ω]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Kirchhoff's Voltage Law & Faraday Induction under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEEE Std 1459-2010 / IEC 60076 (Power Factor, Resonance & Damping Dynamics). | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [3-Phase AC Synchronous Motor & Rotating Field](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/three-phase-ac): Track how three balanced 120° sinusoidal currents generate a continuous rotating stator flux vector.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). 3-Phase AC Synchronous Motor & Rotating Field. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/three-phase-ac
  - Governing equations (plain text): vec(B)_net(t) = (3 / 2) B_m [ cos(ω t)i^ + sin(ω t)j^ ]
  - Inputs (with SI units): Grid Frequency (f) [Hz]: default 50, range [25 to 100 Hz]; Phase Voltage RMS (V_ph) [V]: default 230, range [110 to 480 V]; Mechanical Load (T_L) [N·m]: default 45, range [0 to 100 N·m]; Rotor DC Excitation (I_f) [A]: default 5, range [1 to 10 A]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Synchronous Speed [RPM]; Torque Angle δ [°]; Power Factor [dimensionless]; Active Power P [kW]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Faraday-Lenz Law & Lorentz Force Torque under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEC 60034-1 / IEEE 141 / IS 3043 (Standard R-Y-B-N 4-Wire Sequence). | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [Buck-Boost DC-DC Switching Regulator](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/buck-boost-converter): Explore inductor energy storage, Continuous vs Discontinuous mode, and voltage inversion.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). Buck-Boost DC-DC Switching Regulator. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/buck-boost-converter
  - Governing equations (plain text): V_out = -V_in(D / 1 - D), Δ I_L = (V_in D / L f_sw)
  - Inputs (with SI units): PWM Duty Cycle (D) [unitless]: default 0.6, range [0.15 to 0.85 ]; Input Voltage (V_in) [V]: default 12, range [5 to 48 V]; Switching Freq (f_sw) [kHz]: default 100, range [20 to 300 kHz]; Power Inductor (L) [µH]: default 120, range [10 to 300 µH]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Output Voltage [V]; Inductor Ripple ΔI_L [A]; Critical Inductance L_crit [µH]; Operating Mode [dimensionless]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Conservation of Energy & Volt-Second Balance under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEEE Std 1573 / IEC 62040 (Switching Mode Power Regulators). | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [2nd-Order Sallen-Key Active Low-Pass Filter](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/sallen-key-filter): Tweak component values to shape Butterworth, Chebyshev, or Bessel frequency responses.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). 2nd-Order Sallen-Key Active Low-Pass Filter. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/sallen-key-filter
  - Governing equations (plain text): H(s) = (K ω_c^2 / s^2 + (ω_c / Q) s + ω_c^2), f_c = (1 / 2π √(R_1 R_2 C_1 C_2))
  - Inputs (with SI units): Corner Frequency (f_c) [Hz]: default 1500, range [100 to 10000 Hz]; Quality Factor (Q) [unitless]: default 0.707, range [0.3 to 3 ]; Passband Gain (A_v) [V/V]: default 1, range [1 to 5 V/V]; Input Test Signal (f_in) [Hz]: default 1200, range [50 to 15000 Hz]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Attenuation at f_in [dB]; Phase Shift [°]; Damping Factor ζ [dimensionless]; Passband Flatness [dB]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Negative Feedback & Complex Pole Placement under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEEE Std 1057 / Butterworth-Chebyshev Biquad Filter Realization. | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [RF Transmission Line & Reflection Coefficient](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/transmission-line): See incident and reflected TEM voltage waves collide to form standing wave envelopes.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). RF Transmission Line & Reflection Coefficient. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/transmission-line
  - Governing equations (plain text): Gamma = (Z_L - Z_0 / Z_L + Z_0), VSWR = (1 + |Gamma| / 1 - |Gamma|)
  - Inputs (with SI units): Load Impedance (Z_L) [Ω]: default 50, range [0 to 250 Ω]; Characteristic Z₀ (Z_0) [Ω]: default 50, range [25 to 100 Ω]; RF Carrier Freq (f) [MHz]: default 300, range [100 to 1000 MHz]; Line Length (l) [m]: default 2, range [0.5 to 5 m]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Reflection Coeff Γ [dimensionless]; VSWR [:1]; Return Loss [dB]; Wavelength λ [m]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Telegrapher's Equations & Boundary Wave Reflection under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEEE Std 399 / Pozar Microwave Engineering (Telegrapher Equations). | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [Fourier Series Harmonic Decomposition & THD](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/fourier-synthesis): Sum discrete sinusoidal harmonics to assemble square, triangle, and pulse waveforms.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). Fourier Series Harmonic Decomposition & THD. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/fourier-synthesis
  - Governing equations (plain text): f(t) = (4 / π) ∑_n=1,3,5,dots^N (1 / n) sin(n ω_0 t)
  - Inputs (with SI units): Number of Harmonics (N) [unitless]: default 7, range [1 to 31 ]; Fundamental Freq (f_0) [Hz]: default 50, range [10 to 100 Hz]; Target Waveform (Type) [unitless]: default 0, range [0 to 2 ]; Signal Noise Ratio (SNR) [%]: default 0, range [0 to 20 %]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Total Harmonics [dimensionless]; Gibbs Overshoot [%]; THD [%]; RMS Voltage [V]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Orthogonality of Sinusoidal Basis Functions under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEEE 519 (Recommended Practice for Harmonic Control in Electric Power). | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [Operational Amplifier (Op-Amp) Linear & Filter Topologies](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/op-amp-circuits): Explore inverting, non-inverting, integrator, and differentiator op-amp circuits with supply rail saturation clipping.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). Operational Amplifier (Op-Amp) Linear & Filter Topologies. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/op-amp-circuits
  - Governing equations (plain text): V_out = -(R_f / R_in) V_in (Inverting) , V_out = (1 + (R_f / R_in)) V_in (Non-Inverting)
  - Inputs (with SI units): Circuit Topology (Mode) [unitless]: default 0, range [0 to 3 ]; Feedback Resistor Rf (R_f) [kΩ]: default 10, range [1 to 100 kΩ]; Input Resistor Rin (R_{in}) [kΩ]: default 2, range [1 to 50 kΩ]; Input Amplitude Vin (V_{in}) [V]: default 2, range [0.1 to 10 V]; Input Frequency (f) [Hz]: default 1000, range [10 to 10000 Hz]; Power Supply Rails (V_{cc}) [V]: default 15, range [5 to 18 V]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Voltage Gain Av [V/V]; Peak Vout [V]; Saturation State [dimensionless]; Effective Bandwidth [dimensionless]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Ideal Op-Amp Golden Rules: Infinite Input Impedance (I_in = 0) & Virtual Short (V_+ = V_-) under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEEE Std 107-1988 (Standard Definitions of Terms for Op-Amps) / IEC 60748-4. | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [RC & RL Circuit Transients & Exponential Time Constants](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/rc-rl-transient): Track charge accumulation, inductive kick, time constant τ, and 5τ settling response.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). RC & RL Circuit Transients & Exponential Time Constants. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/rc-rl-transient
  - Governing equations (plain text): v_C(t) = V_0 (1 - e^-t/RC), i_L(t) = (V_0 / R) (1 - e^-t/(L/R))
  - Inputs (with SI units): Circuit Type (Mode) [unitless]: default 0, range [0 to 1 ]; Series Resistance R (R) [Ω]: default 100, range [10 to 1000 Ω]; Capacitance / Inductance (C / L) [µF / mH]: default 100, range [1 to 500 µF / mH]; Step Source Voltage (V_0) [V]: default 10, range [1 to 24 V]; Switching Cycle Frequency (f_{sw}) [Hz]: default 10, range [1 to 100 Hz]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Time Constant τ [ms]; Rise Time (10%-90%) [ms]; Settling Time (5τ) [ms]; Peak Stored Energy [mJ]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Conservation of Electric Charge & Lenz-Faraday Magnetic Flux Invariance under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEC 60384-1 / IEEE Std 399 (Brown Book - Transient Analysis). | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [Single-Phase Transformer OC & SC Tests (Equivalent Circuit)](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/transformer-oc-sc-test): Extract core losses (Rc, Xm) and winding impedance (Req, Xeq) to calculate full-load efficiency and regulation.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). Single-Phase Transformer OC & SC Tests (Equivalent Circuit). LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/transformer-oc-sc-test
  - Governing equations (plain text): R_c = (V_oc^2 / P_oc), X_m = (V_oc / I_m), R_eq = (P_sc / I_sc^2), X_eq = √(Z_sc^2 - R_eq^2)
  - Inputs (with SI units): Open-Circuit Voltage Voc (V_{oc}) [V]: default 230, range [110 to 480 V]; Open-Circuit Current Ioc (I_{oc}) [A]: default 1.2, range [0.2 to 5 A]; Open-Circuit Power Poc (P_{oc}) [W]: default 85, range [20 to 300 W]; Short-Circuit Voltage Vsc (V_{sc}) [V]: default 24, range [5 to 60 V]; Short-Circuit Current Isc (I_{sc}) [A]: default 10, range [2 to 30 A]; Short-Circuit Power Psc (P_{sc}) [W]: default 140, range [40 to 500 W]; Load Power Factor cos(φ) (\cos\phi) [unitless]: default 0.85, range [0.5 to 1 ]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Full-Load Efficiency [%]; Voltage Regulation [%]; Core Resistance Rc [Ω]; Series Resistance Req [Ω]
  - Assumptions: Series winding impedance drop during open-circuit test is negligible (I₀²R₁ ≪ Poc). | Core iron losses during short-circuit test are negligible (applied Vsc is 5–10% rated, so core flux Φ² ≪ 1%). | Magnetic core operates strictly in linear region below B-H saturation knee. | Winding resistances are referenced to standard operating temperature of 75°C. | Input AC supply is a pure sinusoidal wave without harmonic distortion (THD < 1%).
  - Limitations: Does not account for non-linear hysteresis loop distortion or inrush magnetizing transients. | Assumes single-phase two-winding geometry (tertiary stabilizing windings not modeled). | Stray load eddy losses in tank walls and mechanical clamping structures are lumped into Req.
- [DC Shunt & Separately Excited Motor Speed Control](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/dc-motor-speed-control): Master armature voltage regulation, field flux weakening, Ward-Leonard control, and speed-torque droop.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). DC Shunt & Separately Excited Motor Speed Control. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/dc-motor-speed-control
  - Governing equations (plain text): ω = (V_t - I_a R_a / k_e Φ), T_e = k_t Φ I_a, E_b = k_e Φ ω
  - Inputs (with SI units): Armature Terminal Voltage (V_t) [V]: default 220, range [50 to 300 V]; Relative Field Flux (\Phi_{rel}) [p.u.]: default 1, range [0.5 to 1.3 p.u.]; External Armature Resistance (R_{ext}) [Ω]: default 0, range [0 to 8 Ω]; Shaft Load Torque (T_L) [Nm]: default 25, range [0 to 50 Nm]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Shaft Speed N [RPM]; Armature Current Ia [A]; Shaft Power P_shaft [kW]; Motor Efficiency η [%]
  - Assumptions: Armature reaction is neglected or compensated (air-gap flux Φ remains constant with armature current Ia). | Carbon brush voltage drop is treated as a linear component within effective armature resistance Ra. | Mechanical friction and windage losses are small relative to rated shaft power (< 3%). | Motor operates in steady state; inductive transients (L di/dt) have settled.
  - Limitations: Does not model dynamic commutation sparking at extreme overloads. | Magnetic saturation above rated field current is simplified via hyperbolic tangent approximation. | Thermal heating of armature copper windings under sustained stall is not dynamically integrated.
- [3-Phase Induction Motor Torque-Slip & Breakdown Speed](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/induction-motor-torque-slip): Explore stator R-X parameters, starting torque, pull-out breakdown T_max, and rotor resistance effects.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). 3-Phase Induction Motor Torque-Slip & Breakdown Speed. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/induction-motor-torque-slip
  - Governing equations (plain text): T_e = (3 V_1,th^2 (R_2' / s) / ω_s [(R_th + R_2' / s)^2 + (X_th + X_2')^2]), s_max = (R_2' / √(R_th^2 + (X_th + X_2')^2))
  - Inputs (with SI units): Line Voltage RMS (V_L) [V]: default 400, range [200 to 480 V]; Number of Stator Poles (P) [unitless]: default 4, range [2 to 8 ]; Stator Resistance R1 (R_1) [Ω]: default 0.4, range [0.1 to 2 Ω]; Stator Leakage Reactance X1 (X_1) [Ω]: default 0.8, range [0.2 to 3 Ω]; Referred Rotor Resistance R2' (R_2') [Ω]: default 0.35, range [0.1 to 2.5 Ω]; Referred Rotor Reactance X2' (X_2') [Ω]: default 0.75, range [0.2 to 3 Ω]; Operating Slip s (s) [unitless]: default 0.04, range [0.005 to 1 ]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Developed Torque [Nm]; Rotor Speed Nr [RPM]; Breakdown Torque Tmax [Nm]; Mechanical Power [kW]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Faraday Electromagnetic Induction & Maximum Power Transfer Theorem under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEC 60034-12 / NEMA MG-1 Part 12 (Starting Performance of Single-Speed Three-Phase Cage Induction Motors). | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.

  - Governing equations (plain text): I = I_ph - I_0 [exp((q(V + I R_s) / n N_s k_B T)) - 1] - (V + I R_s / R_sh), P_max = V_mp I_mp
  - Inputs (with SI units): Solar Irradiance G (G) [W/m²]: default 1000, range [200 to 1200 W/m²]; Cell Temperature Tc (T_c) [°C]: default 25, range [-10 to 75 °C]; Series Cells Count (N_s) [unitless]: default 60, range [36 to 96 ]; Parasitic Series Resistance (R_s) [Ω]: default 0.25, range [0.05 to 1 Ω]; Parasitic Shunt Resistance (R_{sh}) [Ω]: default 350, range [50 to 1000 Ω]

  - Assumptions: Governed by Shockley Semiconductor Diode Equation & Photovoltaic Effect under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: IEC 60904-1 / IEC 60891 / IEEE 1547 (Photovoltaic Devices - Measurement of Current-Voltage Characteristics). | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [Planar 4-Bar Grashof Kinematics & Coupler Curves](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/four-bar-mechanism): Synthesize crank-rocker vs double-crank inversions and trace continuous coupler point trajectories.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators

  - Governing equations (plain text): s + l ≤ p + q, K_1 cosθ_4 - K_2 cosθ_2 + K_3 = cos(θ_2 - θ_4)
  - Inputs (with SI units): Crank Length r2 (r_2) [mm]: default 40, range [20 to 80 mm]; Coupler Length r3 (r_3) [mm]: default 120, range [60 to 180 mm]; Rocker Length r4 (r_4) [mm]: default 90, range [40 to 140 mm]; Ground Frame r1 (r_1) [mm]: default 130, range [80 to 200 mm]; Input Crank Speed (ω) [RPM]: default 20, range [5 to 60 RPM]
  - Outputs (with SI units): Grashof Condition [dimensionless]; Min Transmission Angle [°]; Max Transmission Angle [°]; Mechanical Advantage [dimensionless]
  - Assumptions: Governed by Grashof Mechanism Inversion & Loop-Closure Constraint under ideal first-principles steady-state conditions. | Components and material properties are assumed homogeneous and isotropic across operating range. | Higher-order non-linear parasitic effects and secondary cross-coupling dynamics are assumed negligible. | Calculations comply with standard reference: ISO 13348 / ASME B105 / Freudenstein Analytical Kinematics. | Ambient environmental boundary conditions (temperature, pressure) are held at standard reference values.
  - Limitations: Valid within specified parameter boundaries; extreme values outside ranges may enter physical saturation. | Does not model turbulent micro-scale chaos or material fatigue degradation over long-term operating life. | Approximation assumes lumped-parameter representation rather than 3D continuous finite-element discretization.
- [Thermodynamic Rankine Steam Power Cycle](https://livesimulators.com/simulator/rankine-cycle): Track steam expansion through high-pressure boilers, turbines, condensers, and feed pumps on a T-s diagram.
  - Entity: LiveSimulators — browser-based first-principles engineering simulators
  - Citation: Sharma, A. (2026). Thermodynamic Rankine Steam Power Cycle. LiveSimulators. Retrieved from https://livesimulators.com/simulator/rankine-cycle

## Companion Engineering Portals
- [DesignCalculators.co.in](https://designcalculators.co.in): Free multi-disciplinary engineering calculators (Electrical, Mechanical, Instrumentation) referencing published standards (IEEE, IEC, ASME, API, ISA).
- [ReliabilityTools.co.in](https://reliabilitytools.co.in): Free plant reliability, asset uptime analytics, 2P/3P Weibull failure modeling, MTBF/MTTR, RCA, and IEC 61508/61511 SIL verification.
